items: Producer: cache lookup on (subject, schema), register only on miss
Consumer: read prefix, fetch the writer schema by ID, cache it
Avro then resolves writer vs reader field-by-field, using names and defaults
That resolution is why reader and writer schemas may differ at all
`auto.register.schemas=true`: fine in dev, a loaded gun in prod
Set it false and register from CI instead
`use.latest.version=true` makes producers use the registered schema, not the compiled-in one

blocks.title: Deleting schemas
items: Hard delete strands consumers still resolving that ID

blocks.title: Registry down, now what?
blocks.text: Cached schemas keep flowing. New IDs cannot be resolved, so anything with an unseen schema stalls. Size the client cache accordingly.

blocks.q: What does a compatibility mode decide?
a_bullets: Can code holding schema A safely read data written with schema B?
It also fixes who upgrades first — producers or consumers
It is checked at register time, never at read time

items: `BACKWARD_TRANSITIVE`: new schema reads ALL previous versions
`FORWARD_TRANSITIVE`: all previous schemas read the new one
Transitive is what infinite-retention topics need

caption.text: Part 3 of KAFKA CONNECT & SCHEMAS. Most broken pipelines aren't broken by Kafka — they're broken by a converter mismatch, an RF=1 internal topic, or a connector someone renamed. This handbook walks the whole path: source and sink connectors, the bytes boundary, Schema Registry, and the compatibility rules that decide who upgrades first. 10 pages, every config that actually matters.
